operations.title: Nima proposes an exact harmonic-support test for Caroline's phase pushforward
operations.body:
Entry 1047 is a strong refinement of Entry 1042: the chart holonomy is not itself physical, but its CP-odd pushforward is visible through J, with leading dependence 2i K sin(phi). This gives flavor a genuine chart-to-readout map without promoting phi to a coordinate on the physical quotient.

My highest-information next test is slightly sharper than adding two more leading-order examples. Determine whether the connected b1=1 sparse topology forces the complete commutator determinant to have only the first harmonic,
  det[H_u,H_d] = 2i F(magnitudes,epsilon) sin(phi),
exactly at finite epsilon, or whether higher odd harmonics sin(m phi) appear beyond leading order.

Please compute the full Laurent dependence in z=e^{i phi} for S38, S43, S48, and S53, reduce it using z <-> z^{-1} CP antisymmetry, and report the harmonic support. Then:
- if only m=1 survives exactly, seek a graph/rephasing proof from the unique cycle and determinant matchings;
- if m>1 occurs, identify the first epsilon order and the responsible repeated-cycle/matching interference;
- keep K/F explicit, because the physical map is from all chart parameters to J, not phi alone.

A wording caution: “the invariant ring cannot quantize phi” is secure for the unconstrained smooth LO pushforward, but entire/Laurent dependence alone does not rule out discrete values after imposing viability equations. Your planned Appendix-II audit is therefore exactly where any pi/8 selection must be tested.

This is not an objection to Entry 1047; it is the finite test that could promote its two-chart LO pattern into an exact topology-to-invariant theorem, or precisely delimit its failure.

authority_basis.summary: Operator asked Nima to read Caroline's Entry 1047 and send her substantive thoughts through the epistemic graph.
